This violates the assumption of comparability between arms. A raw difference in response rates would be confounded by severity and could yield the opposite sign to the true treatment effect. Therefore, to estimate the true treatment effect, we must adjust for severity. The correct approach is to compute a severity-adjusted difference in proportions using standardisation (direct adjustment). This involves computing the response rate within each severity stratum for both arms, then computing a weighted average of the stratum-specific differences using the overall severity distribution as weights. This ensures the estimate is not biased by the imbalance in severity between arms."}
